# Coupled sizing results

<!-- Generated by scripts.publish_coupled_results. -->

**The search has not established a credible minimum-size boat.** The numerical result is limited by a search bracket and the hull-resistance model. It remains an exploratory candidate, not a design recommendation.

The shared-design solve found a screening-feasible candidate: **0.800 m length by 0.650 m beam**, 28.89 kg at the search mesh resolution. Its length/beam ratio is 1.23. The wave-drag approximation depends on Froude number and displacement but lacks adequate hull-form dependence for such broad geometry. Extending its output to this shape is not validated.

Search maximum scaled equilibrium residual: 2.36e-10; minimum normalized margin: -5.85e-10. Numerical convergence does not establish physical applicability.

Active numerical/domain bounds: length_m: lower bracket 0.8; battery_x_fraction: upper bracket 0.35.

## What the coupled calculation changes

The wing uses its CAD section for skin mass, weak-axis stiffness and displaced volume. Both chord orientations supply VSPAERO polars; wing moment affects yaw balance and actuator demand. Motor/gearbox moving losses are separate from holding/controller loads. Tack time fractions cancel crosswind displacement before current and route duration are evaluated.

The old reference wing passes its bending-strength screen but fails the declared tip-deflection allocation with the CAD section. Its generic section approximation was insufficient. The free-design search can adjust area, aspect ratio, thickness, laminate, ballast and actuator ratings together.

## Refined replay and sensitivities

Replay uses finer geometry, re-solves both-tack operating states, and evaluates four mast positions through -180 to 180 degrees with hydrostatic heave and pitch equilibrium. A static pass remains conditional on sealed geometry and the declared physics.

| Scenario | Balanced operating states | Static screens pass | Lowest operating margin | Lowest structural/practical margin | Route time (h) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| nominal | True | True | 0.000 | 0.000 | 67.21 |
| construction | True | False | 0.000 | -0.257 | 68.69 |
| aerodynamic | True | True | 0.000 | 0.000 | 68.62 |
| energy | True | False | -0.600 | 0.000 | 67.21 |
| combined | True | False | -0.600 | -0.257 | 149.24 |

Normalized margins below -0.0001 fail the selected screen; smaller numerical residuals display as zero. Scenario brackets are engineering sensitivities, not measured distributions: see [native inputs](../models/coupled-uncertainty.sysml). Route times use synthetic wind/current exposure; no accepted-weather or ocean qualification is implied.

## Water-ingress recovery sensitivities

| Wing state | Cases restoring at sampled interior angles | Worst restoring moment (Nm) |
|---|---:|---:|
| sealed | 8/8 | 13.30 |
| free_flooding_homogenized | 8/8 | 3.88 |
| full_water_retention | 0/8 | -582.85 |

Each state covers freshwater and seawater at four locked mast positions. Free flooding uses homogenized material buoyancy; full retention fills the estimated void at its volume centroid. These are static loading sensitivities, not predictions of leakage, drainage or slosh. See [recovery data](analysis/coupled-recovery.json).

## Decision

Keep the geometry, native physics and optimization workflow. Resolve hull-resistance applicability and active numerical bounds, then rerun the search and adverse scenarios. The short hull from this run is not selected.

Experimental resistance data such as the [Delft/UCI yacht dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/243/yacht%2Bhydrodynamics) offer a better basis for hull-form dependence, but normalization and geometric applicability must be established before use.

Remaining evidence includes viscous/stall and broadside wing behavior, aerodynamic thickness sensitivity, hull-form resistance, environmental/fouling exposure, selected hardware, laminate/joint properties, ingress/drainage behavior and dynamic recovery. These are separate from numerical solver convergence.
